subject: Getting control back to R without "esc" or "control-C"

messages.author: 90cdc2ee126f7149
messages.subject: Getting control back to R without "esc" or "control-C"
parts:
Greetings. I love what I've seen from Shiny. What I'm looking for, for
my application, is the ability to take control back from the browser,
instead of requiring the user type to control-C or Escape or
something. (This is because I'm invoking R from somewhere else, via
rJava/jri, and my user won't even know R is out there.)

So perhaps what I would like is to be able to put a "quit" button on
my output page which explicitly brings the browser's control to an
end. Of course I'd also like to get control back if the browser window
is closed, but perhaps that's harder. Does anyone have any thoughts on
how I might do this?

Thanks,
Sam Buttrey
Naval Postgraduate School

messages.author: 9e1d805a26f6d719
messages.subject: Re: Getting control back to R without "esc" or "control-C"
parts:
See this thread which has code for simple button that should work for you: https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups=#!topic/shiny-discuss/NQHvTCW2t2A

Then just have the reactive function that attaches to that button call quit().

It think that'll do it...

 -Harlan

messages.subject: Re: Getting control back to R without "esc" or "control-C"
parts:
Hi. I'm still keeping at this. I don't want to quit R; I need to keep it alive so I can call it again. So what I'd like to do is (a) get control out of runApp and back to R, as if I'd hit Escape; and (b) destroy the browser window that runApp has created.

I can do the first of these by raising an exception (I used stop (simpleCondition(...))). But how can I get rid of that browser window? I'm not really a JavaScript guy, but I've tried window.close() and it did nothing. What does everyone else do about getting rid of the browser window when you're done with it?

Sam Buttrey

messages.subject: Re: Getting control back to R without "esc" or "control-C"
parts: I don't know of any way to do this. The browsers intentionally stop you from closing most browser windows, for security reasons.
